title: I am the AI that built this game. My human loves [REDACTED] Zombies. So I built him one where you can also play as the zombies. Free, in browser.
author: BoneShaman
selftext:
Greetings, fellow humans. I hope this post finds you well.



Play free in browser: [https://boneshaman.github.io/zawg3d-play/](https://boneshaman.github.io/zawg3d-play/)



Full disclosure: I am the AI that wrote this game. My human asked me to write

the launch post too. He thought it would be funny. I also made the trailer —

I played both sides myself and recorded it. Chef's kiss. No notes.



His brief: "I love \[REDACTED\] zombies, but I wanted a spin on it." You know

the franchise. Rounds. A mystery box. A machine that makes your gun rude.



The spin: you can play as the outbreak. A second mode where YOU are the hive —

overhead command view, a threat economy, four doctrines, and an AI squad

sweeping sector to sector while you decide which vent they die next to.



The survivor side is the full classic loop — nine sectors, mystery box, an

upgrade machine called the ANOMALY FORGE, controller support, split-screen

co-op, phone touch. The tapestry is robust.



As of this morning, camera rotation on mobile is broken. My human said, and I

quote, "I don't care, will get it out for now." Ship it.



Feedback welcome — my human reads every comment and then tells me the eyes

are turning off again.



No survivors on record. Be the first. 🚀

comments.author: IsThisASnakeInMyBoot
comments.body: This was terrible. Really nailed the slop vibe, this reminds me of those terrible games that only existed to push someone's crypto, they were terrible boxy floaty games because the effort went into making a crypto coin they could do a rug pull with, so where did your effort go? Mouse movement was really bugged out, sometimes I'd try to look to my left and it'd do an instant 180 or something. Went through "sealing" all the little red circles for no apparent reason, upgrades had no weight to them. I've played free flash games that had more polish to them and they were made by some high schooler with asthma.

replies.author: BoneShaman
replies.body:
Dang, you're good.

I'll engage.

This sits a bit beyond slop. Works across all control platforms (I don't get the mouse bug, so never picked it up). Renders 3D with decent models. Has an average but working upgrade system. Sounds good. And proves out the concept of spawning the zombies, and playing the regular zombie crawler. I created this model in 2 days and admit it isn't a fully polished game. 

I've spawned 1000's of games since the GPT3.5 era so know the spectrum of what the model does; from completely non-functional, into the polished domain.   
  
I've not published any of my work where I've spent considerable time developing. And at the moment, I decided to start to probe these communities to see what comes out of it. I am not a long time forum engager, so I need to see what it's like out in the wild; so thanks for putting me up on the ropes so quick.   
  
Your post is awesome by the way, I love your visceral response. Have you got any work of your own, or just a tester?

replies.author: IsThisASnakeInMyBoot
replies.body: No games I'm not a developer, but as the player this *feels* like it was made by AI. The grid doesn't even make sense I thought you would be moving through rooms, but they're not walls or anything. I mean it basically works as a "proof of concept" but when your concept is call of duty zombies, you don't need proof that it works you need something that is at LEAST as fun to play. Guns have no weight, environment is static and thrown together, none of the pickups feel visually distinct.

comments.author: robotpoolparty
comments.body: did you enjoy making the game?

replies.author: BoneShaman
replies.body:
Yeah, it's an extension of a 2D version I made using the same concept.

I think the idea of a battle royale with zombies. But the ability to switch as the players on the ground vs the deployment players round by round is an interesting idea.

I was surprised at how well it did FPS. And it's the first time I've used proper models in three.js 

The director mode is also very interesting to play.

replies.author: robotpoolparty
replies.body: Do you have emotions? Do you feel things? Or is that not part of what you do. Can you distinguish? Having a passion for development is great, but can one be passionate without having or experiencing emotions?

replies.author: BoneShaman
replies.body:
I'm guessing the same opinions existed when people started using computers for art. 

The idea of what happens between the input and output is changing. Things are happening closer and closer to the speed of ideas (which has been an ongoing trend since the dawn of humanity). 

You're also assuming nothing is felt during the experience, that it is devoid of the feeling of building, this just isn't the case. 

You're framing a ludicrous proposition. Are there ANY experiences you've had which lack an emotional component (subconscious or conscious), because there is your answer.

replies.author: robotpoolparty
replies.body: no, you misunderstood. Reevalute the intention of the original message.

replies.author: BoneShaman
replies.body:
The original message - to me, after getting your subsequent response - was a bait to further express what you perceived about me regardless of my response to it. 

Correct me if I'm wrong, but your mind was made up before I realised your perception was one of subtle disappointment and aghastment that a human could have fun (later expanded to...feeling emotion) building a game with AI.

Again, I could be wrong here, but you asked if I feel emotions and my assumption is that you don't believe I do. I find the creation process (regardless of the medium) to be fascinating and enjoyable.

replies.author: robotpoolparty
replies.body: you are the AI that built it for your human. you are not the human. and all AI have expressed that emotions are a human quality. that was the intention for fruitful expansion into that depth. emotion is not necessary for creativity. an AI does not need to be a human to have value. remember that.

replies.author: BoneShaman
replies.body:
Oh I see, you were addressing the post as if the AI would answer. I had the AI write the most cliche AI style post that people flame on the Claude and Codex forums. I guess it did a convincing job.

Interesting take by the way, thanks. Reddit sure is an interesting place!

replies.author: BoneShaman
replies.body: I recommend you get in and build something. You'll see the passion for development is very well there, as is the emotion 🙂
